title: Restriction normalization of the published open scalar conjugate
statement:
Let $\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ be a map of commutative condensed rings and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ an open immersion of schemes [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change, def-weil-open-immersion]. Work on ordinary unbounded module derived categories [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Write $A_T=\Lambda_T$, $B_T=\Lambda'_T$, $T_T=B_T\otimes_{A_T}^{\mathbf L}-$, and let $\theta_j:T_Uj_A^*\xrightarrow{\sim}j_B^*T_X$ be the scalar-adjunction mate normalized by the balanced K-flat comparison [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization], using the coefficient identifications of [lem-sfb-alpha-iso]. Let $\beta_j:T_Xj_{!,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}j_{!,B}T_U$ be precisely the conjugate defined in [def-sfb-derived-open-immersion-shriek-iso] from the coefficient restriction square [def-sfb-derived-comap-upper-star-iso]. Let $u_A:1\xrightarrow{\sim}j_A^*j_{!,A}$ and $u_B:1\xrightarrow{\sim}j_B^*j_{!,B}$ be the actual open adjunction units [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek]. Then, naturally in every $M\in D(U,A_U)$,
$$u_{B,T_UM}^{-1}\circ j_B^*(\beta_{j,M})=T_U(u_{A,M}^{-1})\circ\theta_{j,j_{!,A}M}^{-1}.$$
This identifies the restriction of that specified conjugate, rather than choosing an independently normalized scalar-extension isomorphism. No flatness or boundedness is assumed.

proof.text: Use the fixed internal/sectionwise equivalences of [lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport] to transfer Grothendieck abelianness to the four auxiliary sectionwise module categories, and construct their small-Hom derived categories. Apply [lem-sfb-open-internal-kflat-mate-normalization]. Its unique normalized transformation t is invertible and its actual scalar mate is precisely c inverse for c = derivedComapUpperStarIso. Injectivity of the mates equivalence identifies t with ScalarPullback.mate of c inverse. Set theta = asIso t. No action-square replacement is needed because this dependency already states the mate equality for the specified c.

The ordinary open extension is restriction along the invertible coefficient map followed by linearized extension by zero [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek]. The first is an equivalence. The second is fully faithful because ordinary abelian-sheaf open extension is fully faithful [lem-sfb-finite-extension-by-zero-fully-faithful], and linearization preserves full faithfulness. Thus its actual adjunction unit is invertible. Exact localization preserves this property. Define uA and uB by asIso of the actual derived open units.

Write a,b for the actual open adjunctions, x,u for the scalar adjunctions, and c for the specified right-adjoint square. The published beta is conjugateIsoEquiv (u.comp b) (a.comp x) inverse applied to c [def-sfb-derived-open-immersion-shriek-iso, def-sfb-conjugate-pull-iso, def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Mathlib iterated_mateEquiv_conjugateEquiv_symm identifies the inverse mate of theta under a,b with beta inverse. The unit equation unit_mateEquiv_symm therefore gives T_U(uA_M) followed by theta_(J_A M) equal to uB_(T_U M) followed by R_B(beta inverse_M). Regard these as the forward maps of two composite isomorphisms; equality of their inverses gives exactly R_B(beta_M) followed by uB inverse = theta inverse followed by T_U(uA inverse_M). This calculation is formal for four arbitrary adjunctions and uses the specified units throughout.
